title: Plum and Apricot Duck Sauce
description: Ripe plums simmer with apricot and a little ginger into a smooth, sweet-tart Chinese-American dipping sauce.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/2 tsp total.

steps.title: Soften the plums
steps.text: Chop {pl} into the skillet and add {w}. Cover and simmer for 7–9 minutes until the fruit collapses.

steps.title: Balance the fruit
steps.text: Stir in {ap}, {rv}, {gi} and {a}. Simmer uncovered for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Puree until glossy
steps.text: Take off the heat. Blend the softened fruit until completely smooth and return to a low simmer briefly if it still runs like juice.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Serve warm with duck or chicken, or chill a portion for dipping. The sauce thickens as the plum cools.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/2 tsp coconut aminos in place of 3 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, use 1 teaspoon rice vinegar and omit the ginger. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 48 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 12.3 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 0.6 g fiber, 72 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 45 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 11.4 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 0.6 g fiber, 15 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
